technical_summary: Target index size: baseline 200M vectors (768-1024 dim), horizon 1B+ vectors within 12-18 months.
Vector lifecycle: frequent updates (daily ingestion + TTL for ephemeral content), must support partial reindexing.
Search stack: ANN for recall + CPU/GPU hybrid reranker for top-50 candidates. Rerank latency budget ≤ 40ms.
Batching strategy: client-side batching preferred for bulk ingestion; server-side dynamic batching for queries is required to improve GPU utilization.
Caching: prefix + hot-key caching for top queries; plan to use KV cache to cut p95 by 30-50% on repeated queries.
Model preferences: open models acceptable; preference for Resizable embedder (fp16/quantized) + lightweight cross-encoder for rerank.
Quantization: interested in int8/int4 workflows to reduce storage and inference cost; needs Redwood guidance on quality tradeoffs.
SLOs: 99.9% availability during business hours, clear fallback path to CPU-based endpoints under GPU congestion.
Observability: token-level cost visibility, per-route latency histograms, and rerank delta metrics required for QA gating.
poc_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): ingest 20M sample vectors, run baseline ANN search using Redwood-hosted Dedicated pool; measure recall and p50/p95 latency.
Phase 2 (3 weeks): add reranking step (cross-encoder) on top-20 candidates, measure end-to-end p95 and cost/query; iterate quantization.
Phase 3 (4 weeks): scale to 200M vectors with sharding and KV cache, simulate 3k QPS traffic; validate batching and autoscaling policies.
Success metrics: p95 latency ≤ 80ms after caching; recall@10 within 1-2% of current on-prem baseline; cost/query reduces by ≥30% vs current infra.
pricing_concerns: Wants committed capacity pricing for Dedicated with predictable egress and token pricing for reranker runs.
Evaluating tradeoffs: reserved capacity + burst vs pay-as-you-go for seasonal demand.
Asks for explicit cost model: storage $/mil vectors, inference $/k tokens for reranker, and request-based ANN cost per query.
